To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified novel epitopes in the N‐terminal part of the autoantigen IA2 as well as two novel conformational epitope in the C‐terminial region.
we have identified several novel epitopes of the type 1 diabetes autoantigen IA-2.
we have mapped the major target regions of IA‐2 antibodies in the C‐termini of the intracytosolic domain of IA‐ 2 and have identified a novel conformation‐specific epitope.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel autoantibody‐binding epitopes on the diabetes‐associated protein IA‐2.
the identification of novel autoantigen regions of IA‐2.
the identification of autoantibodies against the tyrosine-phosphatase IA-2 in type 1 diabetic patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N‐termini of IA‐2/IA‐2β are the most important regions for autoantibody generation.
the autoantibody epitopes in IA‐2ic are not restricted to the tyrosine‐phosphatase domain, but are scattered over the whole intracellular part of the molecule.
autoantibodies to IA‐2 recognize a number of conformational epitope clusters, the majority of which is restricted to the intracytoplamic region of IA‐2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we defined novel epitopes for IA‐2, an autoantigen that is associated with type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
IA‐2 is a highly immunogenic protein, which is recognized by a large variety of autoantibodies.
the autoantibodies against IA‐2 are mainly targeting the C‐terminal end of IA‐2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are at least three different types of epitopes in the intracellular region of IA‐2, and these epitopes are important for the development of diabetes.
the autoantibody response to IA‐2 in patients with type 2 diabetes is directed to the same regions of the protein as in patients with type I diabetes.
we have defined several novel autoantigen epitopes in the intracytoplamsic part of the diabetes-associated autoantigen IA-2.
